Date: 09/11/2026
Patient Name: Calvin Morris
DOB: 12/12/1966
MRN: MRN-59395

To: Cardiology Clinic Intake
From: Dr. Paul Ellis, Riverside Family Practice

Dear Colleague,

Reason for referral: Evaluation of an episode of fainting.

I am sending Calvin Morris, a 59-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypothyroidism, to your clinic for evaluation of a brief fainting episode.

He felt lightheaded after standing from a chair, then briefly lost consciousness. He returned to his usual state shortly afterward and reports no prior episodes.

Thank you for seeing this patient.

Dr. Paul Ellis
Riverside Family Practice

SUBJECTIVE:
Calvin Morris is a 59-year-old man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypothyroidism who briefly fainted after standing from a chair. He felt lightheaded beforehand and returned to his usual state shortly afterward. He reports no prior episodes.

VITALS:
BP 135/92, HR 89, RR 16, SpO2 99% on room air, weight 132 lb.

EXAM:
General: well appearing, no distress.
Neck: no jugular venous distension.
Cardiac exam: regular rate and rhythm, normal S1 and S2, no murmurs or gallops.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Extremities: no peripheral edema.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN:
1. Transient fainting after standing, preceded by lightheadedness. Refer to cardiology for evaluation. Advise him to rise slowly and seek urgent care for recurrent fainting, chest discomfort, shortness of breath, or worsening symptoms.
2. Hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypothyroidism. Continue routine follow-up with primary care.
